newsitem.title: UK: Ford says Halewood plant has future.
newsitem.headline: Ford says Halewood plant has future.

text.p: The head of U.S. car giant Ford in Europe said on Wednesday that the company's Halewood plant in northwestern England, where one job in three is to be cut, still has a future.
"Our stated objective, and we feel very strongly about this, is that we want Halewood to remain operating," said Jac Nasser, president of Ford Automotive Operations and Chairman of Ford Europe.
"We will certainly discuss the possibility of grants with the British government," he said in an interview on BBC radio.
"The grants will be based on what needs to happen to be able to support Halewood relative to alternative sources in Europe."
He added: "Halewood, just like any other plant, is really competing for capital. Therefore it's an open competition. It could be anywhere -- eastern Europe, southern Europe."
Union leaders will meet Nasser on Thursday and Friday in an attempt to reverse 1,300 planned job cuts at Halewood, where the Escort model is produced. But Ford is not expected to change its mind.

The unions decided, after talks with Ford's British management last month, to ballot 30,000 car workers on whether to strike in protest at the job cuts. The process is expected to take up to six weeks.

Halewood workers say their costs are lower than Ford plants in Spain or Germany, but they are being targetted because employment legislation makes it easier to dismiss them than workers at plants producing the Escort in Europe.
Transport and General Workers' Union national officer Tony Woodley said: "I believe it is about politics, about being able to sack our people more cheaply than those in Germany or Spain."
Woodley said this was "unfair and unacceptable".
Greg Knight, the industry minister dealing with Ford, confirmed the government was in talks with Ford about Halewood.

But for reasons of commerical confidentiality he was unwilling to agree to demands by the opposition Labour Party, tipped by opinion polls to win the election which must be called by May, to be included in the talks.
"The government wishes to secure the long term future for Halewood. That is the basis of our discussions with Ford," he told the BBC.
Media reports have suggested that a government grant of about 70 million pounds ($112 million) for Halewood is under discussion. ($1=.6237 Pound)
